# Temple Scroll Column 35 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 35 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**35:1** No one who is ritually impure from any bodily contamination may enter My temple until he has been purified.

**35:2** No man with a bodily discharge or who has had a seminal emission may enter My temple.

**35:3** He must wait until he has bathed in water and the sun has gone down — only then may he enter on the next day.

**35:4** No blind person may ever enter, so that My temple is not defiled — for I live among My people there.

**35:5** No one who is lame or who has any permanent physical defect may enter and defile My temple.

**35:6** Warn all the people of Israel about every kind of impurity, so that they do not defile My temple.

**35:7** Any man recovering from a discharge must count seven full days for his purification.

**35:8** On the eighth day he must wash his clothes and bathe his whole body in running water; then he will be clean.

**35:9** Once clean, he may eat the sacred food — for it is his rightful portion.

**35:10** But anyone who has not finished his purification period must not eat any sacred food.

**35:11** He must not set foot in My sanctuary until the full purification period is over.

**35:12** This will keep the Israelites from contaminating themselves while still impure and defiling My temple where I dwell.

**35:13** Any man who has sexual relations with his wife must stay out of the entire temple city for three days.

**35:14** No impure person may be seen anywhere in My temple.

**35:15** Post guards at the temple gates to keep out anyone who is impure.

**35:16** My temple is holy, and the place where I have put My name is holy — it must never be defiled.

---

*PNEUMA notes: This column sets strict purity standards for temple access. The permanent exclusion of people with blindness and lameness goes beyond Torah requirements. The three-day exclusion from the city after sexual intercourse is stricter than the one-day rule in Leviticus 15:18. "Running water" renders the Hebrew for living/flowing water.*
